description: Recorded measurements that back an evidence claim. A capability value cites one as 'measurement:<id>' in its evidence mapping, the same way it cites 'make:<target>' or 'example:<case>'. The difference is what the source is: a make target or example is re-runnable on demand, while a measurement is a run that already happened and cannot be cheaply repeated - a cluster campaign, a refinement study, a reference comparison. Recording it here is what lets a later reader, human or agent, see that the question was already answered, on what, and to what threshold, instead of running it again.

record_contract.id: stable identifier, referenced as measurement:<id> and cited by name in the capability entry
record_contract.question: the single question the campaign was run to answer
record_contract.date: ISO date the measurement was taken
record_contract.commit: repository revision the measurement was taken at
record_contract.environment: machine, scheduler, and rank layout the run actually used
record_contract.configuration: case, grid, and the settings that determine the result
record_contract.result: what was measured, the threshold it was judged against, and the verdict: met, not-met, or inconclusive
record_contract.limitations: what this measurement does not establish; required, and 'none' is not an acceptable value
record_contract.artifacts: committed derived data supporting the result; may be empty when the numbers in 'result' are the whole record

records.question: Does the matrix-free Newton-Krylov momentum path with the frozen_momentum_jacobian point-block preconditioner run production-size curved-duct cases to completion, with every physical step converged and committed and the pressure projection divergence-free, across a three-grid refinement study?

records.configuration: Laminar flow through the Humphrey, Taylor & Whitelaw (1977) square-duct 90-degree bend: grid.gen sweep, unit square cross-section, path straight 5 D, arc radius 2.3 D through 90 degrees, straight 7 D; uniform spacing. Three grids, refined uniformly in all three directions: 32 x 32 x 256, 48 x 48 x 384 and 64 x 64 x 512 cells. Re = 790 (density 1, viscosity 1/790, unit length and velocity). Inlet prescribed_flow with a generated square_duct_poiseuille profile (bulk 1); noslip walls; conservation outlet; streamwise_constant initial condition; no LES, wall function, IBM or particles. Momentum: Newton Krylov, central convection, finite_difference/matrix_free Jacobian, preconditioner frozen_momentum_jacobian with point_block structure, SNES newtonls with backtracking, snes rtol 1e-8 (32-cell grid) or 1e-6 (48 and 64), GMRES ksp rtol 1e-6, max_it 400, restart 80, Eisenstat-Walker adaptive linear tolerance on. Pressure: FGMRES with four-level multiplicative multigrid, coarse level preonly + redundant. dt = 0.02, 0.0133 and 0.01 (streamwise CFL held below 1), 3000, 4500 and 6000 steps, physical time 60 on each grid. Near-wall diffusion number nu*dt/dx^2 is about 0.03 to 0.05.

result.measured: All 13,500 physical steps (3000 + 4500 + 6000) appear in Momentum_Solver_Newton_Krylov_Summary_Block_0.log with no missing or duplicate steps, every one with state committed and the frozen_momentum_jacobian / point_block preconditioner. Termination reasons: CONVERGED_SNORM_RELATIVE 2993 / 3185 / 4426 and CONVERGED_FNORM_RELATIVE 7 / 1315 / 1574 on the 32 / 48 / 64 grids. Newton iterations per step 2 to 5; Krylov iterations per step at most 25 / 19 / 18, median 4, falling from 14-25 at start-up to 3-4 at steady state; largest final nonlinear norm 8.2e-9 / 1.5e-6 / 4.0e-6. Continuity_Metrics.log: maximum divergence over every step 4.60e-10 / 3.37e-10 / 3.13e-10, maximum net boundary flux 1.6e-15 / 2.0e-15 / 8.9e-15. All three runs reached steady state (solution_convergence u_abs_l2 3.6e-9 / 4.5e-9 / 4.9e-9 at the final step) and the solver output reached 100 percent. Exploratory accuracy context, not part of the verdict: against Humphrey, Taylor & Whitelaw (1977) Fig. 2, digitised (299 of 300 points), the streamwise-velocity RMS difference at 0 / 30 / 60 / 90 degrees is 0.074 / 0.182 / 0.177 / 0.135 U_b on the 64 grid; the 48-to-64 change is 0.001-0.013 U_b RMS; a Celik et al. (2008) three-grid analysis on the symmetry plane gives apparent order 1.9-2.7 and absolute GCI_fine at most 0.03 U_b; the experiment's own X_H = -5 profile differs from the exact fully developed solution by 0.078 RMS.
result.threshold: Retrospective production-execution criterion, the same as the one applied to preconditioner none in turbulent-channel-nk-2026-09-29: every inspected physical step converges and commits, pressure-projected divergence stays below 1e-9, and each run completes. Applied during review, not preregistered. Agreement with the experiment is a separate question and is not part of this verdict.

records.limitations: Laminar, steady, low-Re flow in one geometry: the mass term dominates the operator (near-wall diffusion number about 0.03-0.05), which is the regime a same-cell point block is expected to handle. No run with preconditioner none on these cases, so no Krylov-count or wall-time benefit is established and no performance claim is made. The current point block is untested at high Reynolds number on wall-resolved grids: the only such run (Re 40,000, 193 x 193 x 513, diffusion number about 1.1, dt 0.01) collapsed with DIVERGED_LINEAR_SOLVE at step 233, but it was built from 4aafb04, before the transpose fix d4f5944, so it says nothing about the present implementation in either direction. Turbulence models, wall functions, periodic and driven boundaries, IBM and multiblock are not exercised. One rank count and layout; no restart, no scaling study. The wall-face eddy viscosity (issue #8) is irrelevant at stencil width zero and is not tested. The accuracy figures depend on digitised reference data and on station planes placed at the nearest grid k-index (up to 0.76 degrees apart across grids).

records.question: Does the dual-time Picard momentum solver with the multigrid pressure projection reproduce laminar square-duct Poiseuille flow, and at what spatial order?
records.commit: d6fff0f plus the uncommitted 2026-09-18 registry-reset working tree (validation refusals, legacy-flag removal, documentation); no momentum, pressure, particle, or metric numerics differ from d6fff0f
records.environment: Local WSL2 workstation, 12 cores, 7 GB RAM; PETSc 3.20.3 debug build (-O0 -g3) with MPICH; local mpiexec, no scheduler; 2, 4 and 6 ranks for n = 8, 16 and 24
records.configuration: Square duct, unit side, length 2, uniform grid_gen box of n x n x 2n cells for n = 8, 16, 24. Re = 10 (density 10, viscosity 1, U = L = 1). -Zeta INLET prescribed_flow with a generated square_duct_poiseuille source (bulk velocity 1, 101 terms), four noslip WALL faces, +Zeta OUTLET conservation. Constant plug initial field. dt = 0.05 for 120 steps (t = 6, about twelve slowest viscous time constants). Dual Time Picard Jameson RK with the flat_channel template controls (max 50 pseudo steps, residual relative tolerance 1e-3). Poisson fgmres + PCMG, 3 levels (2 for n = 8, see limitations).

result.measured: Streamwise velocity on the mid-length cell plane against the 201-term series at cell centres: relative L2 error 3.49e-2, 9.67e-3, 4.39e-3 (observed order 1.85 then 1.95); relative max error 4.00e-2, 1.09e-2, 4.93e-3. Axial pressure gradient over the middle half against -28.4536/Re: relative error 5.89e-2, 1.54e-2, 6.92e-3 (order 1.93 then 1.98). Inflow equals outflow to 1e-9; maximum divergence at most 5.5e-8; every physical step met its pseudo-time tolerance except one early transient step at n = 24; the steady field changed by less than 2e-10 per step at the end.
result.threshold: Errors decrease monotonically under refinement with observed order at least 1.8 in velocity and pressure gradient.

records.limitations: Steady laminar flow only: temporal order was not measured, and in fully developed duct flow the convective term vanishes, so convection is exercised only by the transient. Uniform Cartesian grid, so the curvilinear metric terms are identity-like; single block; Re = 10. The same duct at Re = 100 with dt = 1.0 hit the 50-iteration pseudo-time cap on every step and finished with an 18% pressure-gradient error, so the result holds only when steps converge. With 3 multigrid levels on the 9-node n = 8 grid the Poisson solve produced NaN; 2 levels were used there.

records.configuration: Re-characterization: the shipped examples/periodic_test/driven_channel/laminar case (Re = 100, 17 x 33 x 17 cells, initial_flux, dt = 0.05) for 10 steps. result.measured: Every Re = 100 step met its pseudo-time tolerance in 9 to 29 iterations (cap 50); the 2026-08-24 stall did not reproduce. At Re = 10 the maximum profile error relative to U_b was 1.81e-2, 5.15e-3, 1.37e-3 (observed order 1.98, 2.00 at the true spacing ratios); the applied force 2.7 x correction / dt matched 3 nu U_b / h^2 to 2.4%, 0.69%, 0.18%; the realized bulk velocity 0.90217, 0.90062, 0.90017 converged to the controller law U_target / (1 + 3 nu dt / (2.7 h^2)) = 0.9. records.configuration: flat_channel duct, programmatic_c 17 x 17 x 33 cells, constant_velocity inlet, conservation outlet, 10 steps with momentum residual tolerance 1e-9 and Poisson relative tolerance 1e-12. Baseline: fgmres, 3 levels, 2 pre and 2 post sweeps, k semi-coarsening, coarse preonly + redundant LU, richardson + bjacobi smoothers. Each variant changed one setting; fields at step 10 were compared with the baseline and the maximum divergence read from Continuity_Metrics.log. cg was also compared with fgmres on the curved bent_channel grid (20 x 20 x 144, 5 steps). The fatal path and the multigrid projection carry unit tests in unit-poisson-rhs.

result.measured: Levels 1 and 2, full coarsening, pre/post sweeps 1/3, chebyshev + jacobi smoothers (169 iterations per step), a Krylov coarse solve (gmres + bjacobi, with its warning), level_1 max_it 4, and cg all reproduced the baseline velocity to at most 7e-15 and gauge-free pressure to at most 8e-14, with divergence at most 5.3e-13. On the curved grid cg matched fgmres to 4.9e-15 and 4.9e-14 with the true residual at 1e-12 or below every step. gmres, lgmres and bcgs failed with left and with right preconditioning: the Krylov residual fell to 1e-12 while the true residual stalled near 1e-3, leaving divergence of 1e-4 to 2.4e-4 and a pressure 3e-5 to 9e-5 off; they are now refused. result.threshold: Each accepted option reproduces the baseline to 1e-10 with divergence below 1e-10; each emitted option is consumed by PETSc.

records.limitations: One duct and one curved grid at small size; the cost of each option was not characterized, and why non-flexible Krylov methods lose the true residual under this preconditioner was not diagnosed beyond the preconditioner not being a fixed linear operator.

records.question: Does the IEM particle update make within-cell scalar variance decay at the model rate 2 Omega, Omega = C_IEM Gamma / V^(2/3), and does the solver's whole decay curve, including cell-to-cell exchange, match an independent implementation of the same discrete step?
records.commit: 3d9b7c1 plus the uncommitted 2026-10-01 working tree (registry and documentation only; no source under src/ or include/ differs from 3d9b7c1); simulator built 2026-10-01 after the last source change
records.environment: Local WSL2 workstation, 12 cores; PETSc 3.20.3 debug build (-O0 -g3) with MPICH; local mpiexec, no scheduler; 2 ranks
records.configuration: examples/brownian_motion adapted: unit cube, 8^3 uniform cells, WALL on every face, ZERO_FLOW analytical carrier, LES off, Gamma = nu/Sc = 1e-3; 32,768 Volume-seeded particles with models.physics.particles.fields Psi = where(uniform() < 0.5, 0, 1). Three runs: C_IEM = 2 (default) with dt = 0.01 for 1000 steps; C_IEM = 20 with dt = 0.01 for 200 steps; C_IEM = 200 with dt = 0.001 for 300 steps; checkpoints every 10 steps. Metric: pooled within-cell variance of Psi from each checkpoint's Psi and CellID, as a ratio to its t = 0 value. Reference: a NumPy emulation of the solver's step order (src/runloop.c: Brownian move, locate, remove particles outside the cube, relax toward the host cell's previous-step scattered mean, scatter), 8 seeds per configuration. Restart: the C_IEM = 20 run continued from its step-100 checkpoint with restart_mode load (picurv run --restart-from) to step 200. Cause of the late-time departure: the C_IEM = 20 run repeated with 131,072 particles (256 per cell, 4 ranks), and emulation variants with frozen particles, with the mean scattered after the move, and with 256 and 1024 particles per cell.

result.measured: Against the emulation, at every output step of all three runs: |z| <= 2.06 (z = solver minus emulation mean, over the emulation's seed standard deviation) and relative difference <= 2.0%, across 1.1 (C=2), 2.1 (C=20) and 2.9 (C=200) decades of variance decay. Against analytic exp(-2 Omega t) while the ratio is above 0.36: within 0.71% in every run. Below that the solver and the emulation both decay more slowly than exp(-2 Omega t), +4.1% at a ratio of 0.08 (C=2, C=20) and +13% at 0.011 (C=200). Cause: IEM leaves cell means unchanged, and particles diffusing across faces carry the differences between neighbouring cell means - here the sampling noise of the random 0/1 start, variance 1/(4 N_pc) - into within-cell variance. With 256 particles per cell the solver's excess falls to +1.1% at a ratio of 0.078 and +4.0% at 0.010 (emulation: +1.0%, +3.75%), and the emulation gives +0.23% and +0.93% at 1024; in the emulation, frozen particles give no excess, and scattering the mean after the move instead of using the previous step's leaves it unchanged (+4.5% against +4.1%). So the departure is variance production by cell-mean differences, falling as 1/N_pc, not a kernel or ordering defect. Restart: the loaded state reproduces the step-100 within-cell variance exactly, and the continued run stays within 0.52% of the uninterrupted run through step 200, the Brownian paths differing because the random stream restarts.
result.threshold: Solver within 3 emulation standard deviations at every output step; analytic rate within 1% over the first e-fold of variance decay. Restart: continued decay within the uninterrupted run's statistical spread.

records.limitations: Zero flow, uniform Cartesian cells and constant Gamma; 2 ranks only. Verifies the implemented update and its coupling to the scatter, not the IEM model: no turbulent flow was run, so C_IEM = 2 and the LES mixing time scale V^(2/3)/(C_IEM Gamma_eff) are not validated against a measured scalar-variance decay. The emulation shares the solver's step order by construction; the fresh-mean variant shows that this ordering does not change the decay in this test, which has no mean flow. Up to 53% of particles left through the walls in the longest run; the pooled metric uses the survivors.

records.question: Does a tanh layer seeded by stability_mode_velocity grow at the Rayleigh growth rate in a PICurv 2D-mode solve, converging with cross-stream resolution?
records.commit: stability-mode-generator branch from c13ba21 (uncommitted at measurement; committed with this record)
records.environment: Local workstation (Intel i7-8750H, 6 cores), PETSc 3.20.3 debug build, 4 ranks.
records.configuration: 2D mode (i frozen), U = 0.5 tanh(y) so dU = 1 and the half-thickness is 1, nu = 1e-4 (Re 1e4 on dU and half-thickness). Box 4 cubic cells in i, cross-stream j on [-15, 15] with no-slip walls, streamwise k over two most-unstable wavelengths (L = 4 pi / 0.4449) periodic with 96 cells. Fundamental (harmonic 2) at amplitude 1e-4, no noise. dt 0.1, Picard dual-time momentum, multigrid Poisson with semi-coarsening in i. Growth from the harmonic-2 Fourier amplitude of the cross-stream velocity at the layer centre, fitted over t = 2 to 10.

result.measured: Eigenvalue growth rate (eigen grid 401 points) 0.09476. result.threshold: Measured growth converging to the Rayleigh eigenvalue under cross-stream refinement.

records.limitations: Two resolutions only, one time step and one Reynolds number; the observed order is from two grids.
